prize_parts.citation: For the discovery of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos with the IceCube observatory, opening neutrino astronomy

statement.case_for: After the full exchange I keep B023 as my preferred single-part prize, but with less certainty than before and with a sharper citation. The deciding criterion for me is the one the committee applies at its best: what did nature tell us that we did not know? IceCube answered a question that thought alone could not settle, and the answer was not a refinement of a known number. A diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos at energies up to the PeV scale exists, it is isotropic enough to include an extragalactic component, and it has been reproduced in several independent analysis channels (through-going muons, cascades, starting events) inside one detector. The citation should rest on the flux and the instrument that made it measurable, and not on TXS 0506+056 or NGC 1068, which are statistically moderate and still await independent confirmation. That wording also answers the chair's question on which achievement is cited: the detector and the flux are inseparable here, and I would say so openly. The trio is a defensible judgement, not a unique solution: Halzen for the AMANDA-to-IceCube concept and leadership, Karle for design, construction and early analysis, Spiering for the science programme and the collaboration. A similar judgement was made for the gravitational-wave prize and it has stood well.
statement.case_against: I have to give the objections their full weight. Attribution in a collaboration of hundreds is not airtight, since AMANDA and DUMAND pioneers sit outside the trio, and I cannot offer a decisive argument for Karle over another founder that is independent of the collaboration's own history. IceCube also has the narrowest base of support among the three front-runners, and a configuration that most of my colleagues would not vote for is not a serious proposal even if I find the physics compelling. Five members now prefer B035 and two prefer B008, and Pearce, who ranked IceCube first in the opening, has moved. I do not treat counts as a scientific argument, but I do treat the reasons given by colleagues who know the detector physics better than a string theorist does. Finally, point-source astronomy is not yet mature, and a committee that wants confirmation from KM3NeT or Baikal-GVD before acting would not be unreasonable.

responses.point: After listening to colleagues he moved from B023 to B035 as his first choice, because it combines strong merit with broad support he can defend, keeping B023 as a second alternative.
responses.response: I understand why you moved, and as chair you are right to ask what can be defended at the end of the process. But the reason you give is the breadth of support, not a new scientific argument against IceCube, and you had earlier said the instrument concept and the diffuse flux were the Nobel-level result. I have not seen that judgement refuted in round 1. Your own adjacency note, that your astroparticle collaborations are close to IceCube, is a reason for you to be careful in advocacy, not a reason for the committee to discount the discovery. I would ask you to say plainly whether your scientific view of B023 has changed or only your estimate of the vote.

responses.point: He prefers B035 as a new way of measuring time, with Katori's concept and first demonstration and Ye's accuracy frontier, but names the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes as the strongest novelty objection and asks whether the lattice clock is distinct.
responses.response: This is the question the chair put to us, and I think you state the objection honestly. The magic-wavelength condition with Lamb-Dicke confinement is a real conceptual step, since it lets a million atoms be interrogated without light-shift, Doppler or recoil errors, and I grant that it is more than a refinement. For a citation to make the distinction explicit it must name the lattice, the magic wavelength and many-atom interrogation, and not the 10^-18 record, which is an achievement of degree. My remaining hesitation is the one I raised in round 1: even so, the result is chiefly a gain in precision on ground the 2005 and 2012 prizes opened, whereas IceCube reports a phenomenon nobody had measured. I do not regard B035 as unsound, and I would support it if the committee judges the instrument-driven discovery case too diffuse.

responses.point: He prefers B008 for a new quantum state of matter, a theory-then-experiment sequence with independent confirmation and a mature two-decade record, and he distinguishes the Z2 classification from the 2016 topological-phase prize.
responses.response: Your distinction is fair, and it moves me somewhat: the Z2 classification and protected helical edge states are not simply the Thouless-Haldane lineage, and the theory-then-experiment pattern is the cleanest on the shortlist. That is why B008 stays my first alternative. Two things still keep it behind B023 for me. First, a second topological prize ten years after 2016 is a judgement call about adjacency, and we should apply the same standard to B008 that we apply to B035 against 2005 and 2012. Second, the attribution cannot be repaired by wording alone: Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed the HgTe system Molenkamp measured, and Fu-Kane-Mele, Moore-Balents and Roy carried the idea to three dimensions. Zhang's death removes one awkward omission but not the question.

responses.point: She prefers B035 because it is calculation and experiment in close agreement, reproduced across many laboratories, but concedes that a topological or tunable-matter discovery may reveal more surprising things about nature than a better clock does.
responses.response: Your last sentence is the heart of my own position, and I appreciate that you stated it against your first choice. I agree that the agreement between atomic-structure theory and experiment at the 10^-18 level is impressive and is exactly the type of check I trust. If we apply the standard of surprise you describe, I would argue it favours IceCube alongside the topological case, since a neutrino flux well above what many expected from known sources was not predicted. I take your point that attribution in B035 is far cleaner than in B023, and that is the most weighty argument against my own choice.

responses.point: He prefers B035, flags that he may need to be cautious on B004 and B012 because of ties to the circuit QED community, and previously doubted that Karle fits the IceCube trio.
responses.response: Thank you for the clear disclosure and for supporting a configuration where you have no stake. On the point of Karle, I still lack an argument that distinguishes him from other founders independently of the collaboration's history, so I would suggest the committee ask for an expert report on the early IceCube design and analysis roles before any vote, which as Secretary I can commission. I also note that B004 is no longer on any member's preferred list, so the recusal question is largely moot for the vote we are heading toward.

uncertainties: Whether an expert report can settle Karle's role relative to other IceCube, AMANDA and DUMAND founders, and whether the committee accepts that a trio inside a large collaboration is a judgement and not a unique solution.
Whether the committee will see the diffuse flux and the detector as the cited achievement, which I believe, or insist on the source associations, which I do not.
Whether KM3NeT or Baikal-GVD will confirm the diffuse flux and the TXS 0506+056 or NGC 1068 associations independently, and whether that should affect timing.

Whether the lattice clock is a distinct invention in the sense we need after the 2005 and 2012 prizes, and how the redefinition of the second should influence timing; I regard it as attractive but not necessary.
Whether the 2016 topological-phase prize weighs against B008 under the same standard of adjacency that is applied to B035.
statement.conflict_note: No change to my round-1 disclosure. No shortlisted candidate is a supervisor, close collaborator or Uppsala colleague, and I have no stake in any ballot. As Secretary I commission outside expert reports, and as a string theorist I depend on experts for the detector and condensed-matter claims. I note Pearce's disclosed astroparticle adjacency to B023 and Johansson's and Olsson's disclosures, and have no objection to any member taking part in discussion if they are open about it.
